## Define workflows in terms of rules

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{.python}
rule mytask:
    input:
        "data/{sample}.txt"
    output:
        "result/{sample}.txt"
    log:
        "logs/{sample}.log"
    params:
        threshold = 0.05
    resources:
        mem_mb = 2_000,
        runtime = 30
    shell:
        "some-tool --threshold {params.threshold} "
        "{input} > {output} 2> {log}"
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

```{.python code-line-numbers="1|2-3|4-5|6"}
rule align:
    input:  "fastq/{sample}.fq.gz"
    output: "bam/{sample}.bam"
    threads: 8

    conda:  "envs/bwa.yaml"
    shell:  "bwa mem -t {threads} ref {input} | samtools sort -o {output}"
```

## Wildcards → DAG → dry-run

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
You request **an output file** → Snakemake recurses back through rules until it hits files that exist. The DAG is built **statically**.

```bash
snakemake results.txt --dry-run
snakemake --rulegraph | dot -Tsvg > rules.svg
```

</div>

## Static DAG breaks down → checkpoints

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
**Problem.** When a step's outputs are only knowable **at runtime** — *e.g.* "split a multi-sample VCF into one file per detected sample" — the static DAG can't list them up-front.

**`checkpoint`** lets Snakemake **pause, re-evaluate the DAG**, and continue with the outputs that just appeared.

```{.python style="font-size: 0.78em;"}
checkpoint split_vcf:
    input:  "cohort.vcf"
    output: directory("per_sample/")
    shell:  "bcftools +split {input} -Oz -o {output}"

def aggregate(wildcards):
    d = checkpoints.split_vcf.get().output[0]
    samples = glob_wildcards(f"{d}/{{s}}.vcf.gz").s
    return expand(f"{d}/{{s}}.stats", s=samples)

rule all:
    input: aggregate
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-alert" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Replaces the legacy `dynamic()` — removed in v8.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%| echo: false
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart TD
  A["rule all"] --> AGG["aggregate (input fn)"]
  AGG -. re-evaluates DAG .-> CP["checkpoint split_vcf"]
  CP --> S1["sample_A.stats"]
  CP --> S2["sample_B.stats"]
  CP --> S3["sample_…N.stats"]
  S1 --> AGG
  S2 --> AGG
  S3 --> AGG
  classDef cp fill:#fef5e7,stroke:#E67E22,color:#6e3906,stroke-width:2px;
  classDef leaf fill:#e8f5f0,stroke:#208F6E,color:#0f3a30;
  classDef agg fill:#f4ecf7,stroke:#8E44AD,color:#4a235a,stroke-dasharray: 4 3;
  class CP cp
  class S1,S2,S3 leaf
  class AGG,A agg
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.72em; color: #7f8c8d; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.2em;"}
DAG is re-resolved after the checkpoint completes — fan-out is discovered, not declared.
:::
:::
:::

## Reproducibility & provenance

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E;"><i class="mdi mdi-anvil"></i>&nbsp; Per-rule software · 3 options</h4>

```python
rule call_snvs:
    conda:      "envs/gatk.yaml"
    container:  "docker://broadinstitute/gatk:4.5"
    envmodules: "GATK/4.5"
    shell: "gatk HaplotypeCaller ..."
```
Pick one or compose (`--sdm conda apptainer`).
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #208F6E;"><i class="mdi mdi-file-document"></i>&nbsp; Reports — auto since 9.1</h4>

```bash
snakemake --report report.html --report-after-run
```

```{.python style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
rule plot_qc:
    input:  "qc/{s}.tsv"
    output: report(
        "plots/{s}.svg",
        caption="report/qc.rst",
        category="QC",
        subcategory="Per cell",
        labels={"sample": "{s}"},
    )
    script: "scripts/plot_qc.py"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.72em; color: #7f8c8d; margin-top: 0.2em;"}
`--report-after-run` (v9.1, Mar 2025) — no manual second run.
:::
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 0.8em; padding: 0.7em 1em; background: #e8f5f0; border-left: 4px solid #208F6E; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.78em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-flask-outline" style="color: #208F6E;"></i>&nbsp; **Report / logger / scheduler plugins** — early ecosystem · *small fraction of nf-core's `nf-prov` reach*

- **report** — `rocrate` (RO-Crate, Leo et al. PLOS ONE 2024) · `nanopub` *(both still WIP, not on PyPI as of Q2 2026)*
- **logger** — [`snkmt`](https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-plugin-catalog/plugins/logger/snkmt.html) (SQLite TUI dashboard) · [`stomp`](https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-plugin-catalog/plugins/logger/stomp.html) (STOMP message bus)
- **scheduler** — [`firstfit`](https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-plugin-catalog/plugins/scheduler/firstfit.html) (first-fit-decreasing alternative to ILP)

<i class="mdi mdi-information"></i>&nbsp; Honest take: most plugins are 1-author, < 100 stars. Compared to nf-core's `nf-prov`, the provenance story is **promising but still early**.
:::

## Monolith → plugin framework

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

<h3 style="color: #8E44AD;"><i class="mdi mdi-package-variant-closed"></i>&nbsp; v7 (monolith)</h3>

All executors, all remote-storage backends, all software-deployment options shipped in **one package**.

```bash
snakemake --use-conda \
          --use-singularity \
          --cluster "sbatch ..."
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<h3 style="color: #8E44AD;"><i class="mdi mdi-puzzle"></i>&nbsp; v8 / v9 (plugins)</h3>

Engine + **5 plugin types**, each pip-installable:

- <i class="mdi mdi-server"></i>&nbsp; **Executor** — slurm, k8s, googlebatch …
- <i class="mdi mdi-database"></i>&nbsp; **Storage** — fs, s3, gcs, zenodo …
- <i class="mdi mdi-text-box"></i>&nbsp; **Logger** — snkmt …
- <i class="mdi mdi-file-document"></i>&nbsp; **Report** — rocrate, nanopub …
- <i class="mdi mdi-clock-fast"></i>&nbsp; **Scheduler** — greedy, ilp, milp
:::
:::

## Storage — in practice

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-database"></i>&nbsp; Concrete: a reference + run from S3</h4>

```{.python}
storage s3_aws:
    provider="s3",
    max_requests_per_second=10,
    endpoint_url="https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com"

rule align:
    input:
        reads = storage.s3_aws("s3://my-bucket/run42/{sample}.fq.gz"),
        ref   = storage.s3_aws("s3://refs/hg38.fa")
    output:
        storage.s3_aws("s3://my-bucket/run42/{sample}.bam")
    threads: 8
    conda:     "envs/bwa.yaml"
    container: "docker://biocontainers/bwa:0.7.17"
    shell:
        "bwa mem -t {threads} {input.ref} {input.reads} | "
        "samtools sort -o {output}"
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-flash"></i>&nbsp; Workflow-wide</h4>

```bash
snakemake \
  --default-storage-provider s3 \
  --default-storage-prefix s3://bucket/run42/
```

<div style="margin-top: 0.8em; padding: 0.5em 0.8em; background: #f4ecf7; border-left: 4px solid #8E44AD; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.85em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-information"></i>&nbsp; Storage plugins available: <code>fs</code> · <code>s3</code> · <code>gcs</code> · <code>azure</code> · <code>http</code> · <code>ftp</code> · <code>zenodo</code> · …
</div>

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; padding: 0.5em 0.8em; background: #e8f5f0; border-left: 4px solid #208F6E; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-tag"></i>&nbsp; v9.18: storage plugins now expose **checksums** → cross-workflow caching is correctness-safe
</div>
:::
:::

## Software deployment — one flag

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin-top: 0;">v7 — many flags</h4>
```bash
--use-conda
--use-singularity
--use-envmodules
--conda-frontend mamba
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
<h4 style="color: #8E44AD; margin-top: 0;">v8 / v9 — one flag</h4>
```bash
--sdm conda         # conda env per rule
--sdm apptainer     # Apptainer/Singularity
--sdm env-modules   # HPC env-modules (EESSI…)
--sdm conda apptainer    # compose
```
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 1em;"}
**Per-rule directives — all three are supported simultaneously:**
:::

```{.python}
rule align:
    conda:      "envs/bwa.yaml"                  # ◀ conda
    container:  "docker://biocontainers/bwa:0.7.17"  # ◀ container
    envmodules: "BWA/0.7.17", "SAMtools/1.18"    # ◀ env-modules
    shell: "bwa mem ..."
```

::: {style="margin-top: 0.6em; font-size: 0.82em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-information" style="color: #8E44AD;"></i>&nbsp; `--conda-frontend mamba` **removed** — `libmamba` is the default solver · Pixi backend on the roadmap.
:::

## What actually matters in v9.x

::: {.v9-grid}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.v9-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-puzzle v9-icon"></i>
<div class="v9-title">Plugins</div>
<ul>
<li>5 categories: exec, storage, **logger**, **report**, **scheduler**</li>
<li>plugins without settings <em>auto-deploy</em></li>
</ul>
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.v9-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-cached v9-icon"></i>
<div class="v9-title">Performance &amp; cache</div>
<ul>
<li>storage-plugin **checksums** → cross-workflow caching is correctness-safe</li>
<li>**named multi-output** caching</li>
<li>auto-detected network FS type</li>
</ul>
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.v9-card}
<i class="mdi mdi-shield-check v9-icon"></i>
<div class="v9-title">Provenance</div>
<ul>
<li>**`--report-after-run`** (9.1) auto-generates the HTML</li>
<li>**RO-Crate** &amp; **nanopub** report plugins *(WIP)*</li>
</ul>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns style="margin-top: 1em;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.v9-card .v9-card-wide}
<i class="mdi mdi-tools v9-icon"></i>
<div class="v9-title">Developer UX</div>
<ul>
<li>`profile.yaml` is the new default filename · pass a YAML file directly</li>
<li>`subpath(with_suffix=...)` helper</li>
<li>**pluggable metadata persistence** — `.snakemake/` to files *or* DB</li>
</ul>
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.v9-card .v9-card-warn}
<i class="mdi mdi-package-variant-closed-remove v9-icon"></i>
<div class="v9-title">The plugin tax</div>
<ul>
<li>each workflow now ships a list of `pip install snakemake-{executor,storage,logger,report}-plugin-*`</li>
<li>plugin versions are **independent** from core → pin all of them, or `snakemake --version` doesn't tell you anything</li>
<li>conda recipes lag · CI envs must be rebuilt when any plugin breaks</li>
</ul>
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Backward-compatibility is the real footgun

::: {style="font-size: 0.92em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
The API moves faster than user pipelines. Same Snakefile, different minor → different behaviour.
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #C0392B; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-close-circle"></i>&nbsp; Removed / renamed</h4>

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
- `dynamic()` outputs → **checkpoints**
- `version:` directive → `conda:` / `container:`
- `subworkflow:` → `module:` + `use rule …`
- `from snakemake.remote.*` → `storage` directive
- v7 profiles silently broken on v8 (removed flags)
:::

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; padding: 0.6em 0.8em; background: #fdecea; border-left: 4px solid #C0392B; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>CI / containers</b> — the legacy "fat" `snakemake` package no longer ships executors. Your Dockerfile / conda env now needs `snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm` (and friends) listed **explicitly**, or `--executor slurm` exits with *"plugin not found"*.
</div>
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-alert"></i>&nbsp; Real case — mosaicatcher</h4>

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}
**Sequential checkpoints** — *e.g.* `mosaic_count → summarise_ploidy → filter_bad_cells` — exercise the DAG-reevaluation path harder than most pipelines.
:::

<div style="margin-top: 0.4em; padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>v8</b> — never reached a working state for our chained checkpoints (DAG re-eval bug on the second checkpoint).<br/>
<b>v9</b> — works · but **some 9.x point releases** silently regress on the same DAG (e.g. group jobs + checkpoint interactions) → we pin a known-good range.
</div>

<div style="margin-top: 0.4em; padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #f4ecf7; border-left: 4px solid #8E44AD; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-lightbulb-on" style="color: #8E44AD;"></i>&nbsp; **Lesson:** treat the engine like a dependency — pin `snakemake==9.X.Y`, pin **every plugin**, gate upgrades on the full test matrix.
</div>
:::
:::

# {.section-divider background-color="#1F3A5F"}

::: {style="text-align: center; padding-top: 1em;"}
<div style="background: white; display: inline-block; padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 18px; vertical-align: middle;">
  <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/33450111?s=120&v=4" style="height: 80px; border-radius: 10px;" alt="Snakemake"/>
</div>
<span style="font-size: 2.6em; color: #fff; margin: 0 0.6em; vertical-align: middle; font-weight: 700;">vs</span>
<div style="background: white; display: inline-block; padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 18px; vertical-align: middle;">
  <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6698688?s=120&v=4" style="height: 80px; border-radius: 10px;" alt="Nextflow"/>
</div>

<h1 style="color: #fff; margin-top: 0.8em;">vs Nextflow</h1>
:::

## The deepest difference — dataflow

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

<h3 style="color: #1F3A5F; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-arrow-up-bold-circle"></i>&nbsp; Snakemake — **pull**</h3>

> Reason **from the end**.

```{.python style="font-size: 0.78em;"}
rule all:
    input: "vcf/cohort.vcf"  # ◀ the target

rule call:
    input:  "bam/{s}.bam"
    output: "vcf/{s}.vcf"

rule align:
    input:  "fq/{s}.fq.gz"   # ◀ leaf
    output: "bam/{s}.bam"
```
*"To produce `cohort.vcf` I need `bam/*.bam`, which needs `fq/*.fq.gz`."* Static DAG.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<h3 style="color: #1F3A5F; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-arrow-down-bold-circle"></i>&nbsp; Nextflow — **push**</h3>

> Reason **from the start**.

```{.groovy style="font-size: 0.78em;"}
workflow {
  reads_ch = Channel.fromFilePairs(
    'fq/*_{1,2}.fq.gz'          // ◀ the source
  )
  bam_ch = ALIGN(reads_ch)
  vcf_ch = CALL(bam_ch)
  vcf_ch.view()
}

process ALIGN { input: tuple val(id), path(reads)
                output: tuple val(id), path("${id}.bam")
                script: "bwa mem ref ${reads} | samtools sort -o ${id}.bam" }
process CALL  { /* bam → vcf */ }
```
*"FASTQ pairs emit into a channel → ALIGN consumes them → CALL consumes ALIGN's output…"* Dynamic DAG.
:::
:::

## Resume / cache — myth-buster

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 0.95em; color: #1F3A5F; margin-bottom: 0.6em; font-weight: 500;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-help-circle" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; *"My input file changed. Will the job rerun?"*
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.rerun-card .rerun-smk}
<h4><i class="mdi mdi-snake"></i>&nbsp; Snakemake — `--rerun-triggers`</h4>

| Signal | Default |
|---|---|
| `mtime` of inputs | ✅ |
| `params` value | ✅ |
| `input` set | ✅ |
| `software-env` hash | ✅ |
| `code` of rule | ✅ |

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
Override per run: `--rerun-triggers mtime params input` &nbsp;·&nbsp; opt-out individually.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.rerun-card .rerun-nf}
<h4><i class="mdi mdi-source-branch"></i>&nbsp; Nextflow `-resume`</h4>

| Signal | Default | `cache 'deep'` |
|---|---|---|
| file **path** | ✅ | ✅ |
| file **size** | ✅ | ✅ |
| file **mtime** | ✅ | — |
| file **SHA-256** | — | ✅ |
| process script | ✅ | ✅ |

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
The popular *"content-hashed by default"* claim is **partially false** — content hashing is opt-in via `cache 'deep'` on the process.
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 0.6em; padding: 0.5em 0.9em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.82em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-information"></i>&nbsp; **Bottom line.** Both tools default to **metadata-based** invalidation. Snakemake's surface area is wider (`code`, `params`, `software-env`); Nextflow's `cache 'deep'` is the only way to get true content hashes.
:::

## Software & containers

| <i class="mdi mdi-format-list-checks" style="color: #1F3A5F;"></i>&nbsp; Capability | <i class="mdi mdi-snake" style="color: #208F6E;"></i> Snakemake | <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/logos/master/nf-core-logos/nf-core-logo-square.svg" style="height: 18px; vertical-align: middle;"/>&nbsp; Nextflow / nf-core |
|---|---|---|
| <i class="mdi mdi-tag-multiple"></i>&nbsp; Per-rule env | `conda:` + `container:` + `envmodules:` | `conda` + `container` directive |
| <i class="mdi mdi-layers-triple"></i>&nbsp; Compose | `--sdm conda apptainer` | engine + conda |
| <i class="mdi mdi-warehouse"></i>&nbsp; Curated registry | snakemake-wrappers | BioContainers · mulled · **Seqera Containers** |
| <i class="mdi mdi-hammer-wrench"></i>&nbsp; Build on demand | — | **Wave** |
| <i class="mdi mdi-folder-network"></i>&nbsp; POSIX over object storage | — | **Fusion** |

::: {.columns style="margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<div style="padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #e8f1f8; border-left: 4px solid #2980B9; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>Wave</b> — Seqera's container-provisioning service. Takes a conda spec attached to a process, **builds an OCI container on demand** with that environment, caches it in a registry. Supports `amd64` + `arm64`. **Apache-2.0, open source.**
</div>
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
<div style="padding: 0.55em 0.8em; background: #fef5e7; border-left: 4px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.78em;">
<b>Fusion</b> — a virtual **POSIX layer** that lets processes read/write S3, GCS or Azure Blob as if they were a mounted directory. Avoids stage-in/stage-out copies on cloud. **Commercial**, part of Seqera Platform.
</div>
:::
:::

## Five pillars

<div class="pillars-table">
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-cached pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Workflow caching</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">SNAKEMAKE_OUTPUT_CACHE</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-cube-outline pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Container caching</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">apptainer-prefix</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-database pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Storage staging</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">fs plugin · scratch</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-group pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">Grouping &amp; arrays</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">group · slurm-array-jobs</code></div>
<div class="pillar-row"><i class="mdi mdi-package-variant pillar-cell-icon"></i><div class="pillar-cell-name">EESSI / env-mods</div><code class="pillar-cell-code">--sdm env-modules</code></div>
</div>

## 1 · Caching — workflow + containers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22;"><i class="mdi mdi-cached"></i>&nbsp; Workflow output cache</h4>

```bash
export SNAKEMAKE_OUTPUT_CACHE=\
  /scratch_cached/<group>/snakemake_cache
```

Per rule:
```python
rule index_ref:
    output: "ref.fa.bwt"
    cache: True   # shared across users
```

Computed indexes (BWA, STAR, ref dicts) reused across users → minutes saved per run.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22;"><i class="mdi mdi-docker"></i>&nbsp; Container & conda cache</h4>

```yaml
# profile
conda-prefix:     /g/<group>/shared/conda
apptainer-prefix: /g/<group>/shared/apptainer
```

<i class="mdi mdi-folder-lock" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Group-writable, `chmod 2775` (setgid) → no per-user re-solves.

<i class="mdi mdi-rocket" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Pre-warm: `snakemake --conda-create-envs-only`
:::
:::

## 2 · Storage — staging via `fs` plugin

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{.yaml filename="profile/config.yaml"}
executor: slurm
default-storage-provider: fs              # local FS-as-storage
local-storage-prefix: /scratch/$USER/wf   # where staged copies land
remote-job-local-storage-prefix: /tmp/$USER/wf

# What stays on shared FS vs. gets staged
shared-fs-usage:
  - persistence            # .snakemake/ metadata
  - software-deployment    # conda/apptainer
  - sources                # the Snakefile itself
  # NOT input-output → staged via fs plugin

# fs-plugin specific
storage-fs-default-osfs: false   # use OSFS not MemoryFS
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin-top: 0;"><i class="mdi mdi-file"></i>&nbsp; Tier each data class</h4>

| Data | Tier | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Reference & indexes | Cached parallel FS | Read 100× |
| BAM / CRAM intermediates | Parallel FS | Sequential writes |
| Conda · containers | Parallel FS (shared) | Multi-user reuse |
| Sorting · temp buffers | **Local scratch** | Per-job, ultra-fast |

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em; margin-top: 0.4em; color: #7f8c8d;"}
CLI ref: `--default-storage-provider` · `--local-storage-prefix` · `--remote-job-local-storage-prefix` · `--shared-fs-usage`<br/>
Plugin ref: [`storage/fs`](https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-plugin-catalog/plugins/storage/fs.html)
:::
:::
:::

## 3 · Job grouping — map · sort · dedup · index → one job

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{.python}
rule bwa:
    input:  "fq/{s}.fq.gz"
    output: temp("bam/{s}.sort.bam")
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"

rule sort:
    input:  "bam/{s}.sort.bam"
    output: temp("bam/{s}.sorted.bam")
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"

rule dedup:
    input:  "bam/{s}.sorted.bam"
    output: temp("bam/{s}.dedup.bam")
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"

rule index:
    input:  "bam/{s}.dedup.bam"
    output: "bam/{s}.bam.bai"
    group:  "alignment_per_cell"
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<div class="slurm-viz">
<div class="slurm-header"><i class="mdi mdi-server-network"></i>&nbsp; <b>1 SLURM job per sample</b></div>
<div class="slurm-step">bwa mem</div>
<div class="slurm-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="slurm-step">samtools sort</div>
<div class="slurm-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="slurm-step">mark_duplicates</div>
<div class="slurm-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="slurm-step">samtools index</div>
</div>

::: {style="margin-top: 0.7em; font-size: 0.78em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-lightbulb-on" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Shared scratch · zero stage-in between steps · `temp()` cleaned at group end
:::
:::
:::

## 4 · Job arrays — pack 1-CPU tasks into one SLURM submission

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.yaml filename="profile/config.yaml"}
executor: slurm
slurm-array-jobs: all       # all eligible rules
slurm-array-limit: 1000     # tasks / array

# pack 10 single-CPU jobs into one array
group-components:
  - count_cell=10
```

For a per-cell rule that needs **1 CPU each**:

```python
rule count_cell:
    input:  "bam/{cell}.bam"
    output: "counts/{cell}.tsv"
    threads: 1
    group:   "count_cell"     # ← the array
```

What lands on SLURM:

```bash
$ squeue -u $USER
JOBID         NAME       NCPUS  ST
12345_[1-10]  count_cell    1   PD
# 1 sbatch · 10 tasks · 1 cpu each
# but SLURM sees a 10-cpu allocation
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<div class="slurm-viz">
<div class="slurm-header"><i class="mdi mdi-server-network"></i>&nbsp; <b>1 sbatch · 10 array tasks · 10 cpus total</b></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 1</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell A</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 2</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell B</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 3</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell C</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">…</span><span class="array-step">…</span></div>
<div class="array-row"><span class="array-tag">task 10</span><span class="array-step">1 cpu · cell J</span></div>
</div>

::: {style="margin-top: 0.6em; font-size: 0.76em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-lightbulb-on" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Big win for **many short single-CPU jobs** (per-cell QC, per-chrom split) — one scheduler decision instead of N.

<i class="mdi mdi-alert" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Heterogeneous resources → don't mix into one array.
:::
:::
:::

## 5 · EESSI — env-modules with native optimisation

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**EESSI** = European Environment for Scientific Software Installations — a CernVM-FS stream of pre-built scientific software, **EasyBuild-compiled per microarchitecture** and mountable on any HPC.

```bash
source /cvmfs/software.eessi.io/versions/2023.06/init/bash
module load BWA SAMtools STAR
```

Per rule:
```python
rule align:
    envmodules: "BWA/0.7.17", "SAMtools/1.18"
    shell: "bwa mem ... | samtools sort ..."
```
Invoke with `--sdm env-modules`.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<i class="mdi mdi-rocket-launch" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; **No conda solve · no image pull** — first job starts immediately

<i class="mdi mdi-chip" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; **CPU-tuned builds** — `zen3`, `icelake`, `haswell` … binaries dispatched per node → measurable wallclock wins on AVX-heavy tools

<i class="mdi mdi-earth" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; **Identical tool versions across sites** (any HPC mounting `/cvmfs`)

<i class="mdi mdi-shield-check" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Reproducibility comparable to containers, without the I/O overhead

<i class="mdi mdi-cash-multiple" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; Zero per-user env duplication on `/g/<group>/shared/conda` → saves quota

[eessi.io](https://www.eessi.io)
:::
:::

## Bonus · dependency cooldowns

::: {style="font-size: 0.88em; margin-bottom: 0.6em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-shield-lock" style="color: #E67E22;"></i>&nbsp; **Why now:** supply-chain attacks on PyPI / npm have **accelerated** since coding agents started auto-resolving dependencies — a single `pip install` invoked by an LLM-driven CI run can pull a maliciously-published patch version minutes after it hits the index. Malicious releases are usually **yanked within hours to days**; cooldowns make compromised versions disappear before your build sees them.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-bottom: 0.6em; color: #6e3906; background: #fdebd0; padding: 0.4em 0.7em; border-left: 3px solid #E67E22; border-radius: 4px;"}
Recent incidents: `ultralytics` (Dec 2024), `xz-utils` backdoor (2024), `lottie-player` npm (Oct 2024), `chalk`/`debug` (Sep 2025), repeated typosquats. **All** would have been blocked by a 7-day cooldown.
:::

::: {.columns style="margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin: 0 0 0.4em;"><i class="mdi mdi-language-python"></i>&nbsp; pip 26.1 *(Apr 2026)*</h4>

```{.bash}
pip install \
  --uploaded-prior-to=P7D \
  requests
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
- 26.0 → absolute date · 26.1 → relative
- Also configurable in `pip.conf`
- Uses PEP 700 upload-time data
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #E67E22; margin: 0 0 0.4em;"><i class="mdi mdi-package-variant"></i>&nbsp; Pixi · `exclude-newer`</h4>

```{.toml}
[workspace]
exclude-newer = "14d"

[exclude-newer]
openssl = "0d"
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
- Per-channel & per-package overrides
- Same concept as uv / rattler
:::
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em; margin-top: 0.6em; color: #7f8c8d; text-align: center;"}
7 days is the commonly cited default · [Richard Si — *What's new in pip 26.1*](https://ichard26.github.io/blog/2026/04/whats-new-in-pip-26.1/)
:::

# {.section-divider background-color="#16A085"}

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-file-cog" style="font-size: 4em; color: #fff;"></i>

<h1 style="color: #fff;">Real EMBL profile</h1>
:::

## Real EMBL profile {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.yaml filename="config.v9+.yaml — execution & resources"}
executor: slurm
jobs: 150

default-resources:
  - mem_mb=500
  - runtime=600
  - slurm_partition='htc-el8'      # EMBL partition
  - constraint=''                  # SLURM --constraint

# Pin alignment to milan nodes (AVX2 path in sambamba)
set-resources:
  ashleys_bwa_strandseq_to_reference_alignment:
    constraint: milan
    slurm_partition: htc-el8
  ashleys_samtools_sort_bam:
    constraint: milan
  ashleys_mark_duplicates:
    constraint: milan
  index_input_bam:
    constraint: milan

# Scheduler hygiene
max-jobs-per-second: 10
max-status-checks-per-second: 10
latency-wait: 60
local-cores: 32

keep-going: true
rerun-incomplete: true
retries: 4                         # attempt-based mem scaling
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{.yaml filename="config.v9+.yaml — software & storage"}
software-deployment-method: [conda, apptainer]
conda-frontend: conda

# Shared caches (group-writable, setgid 2775)
conda-prefix:     /g/korbel2/shared/conda_envs
apptainer-prefix: /scratch/korbel/shared/apptainer_cache
apptainer-args:   "-B /g,/scratch,/scratch_cached,/tmp"

# Storage staging (off when data already on /scratch)
default-storage-provider: none
local-storage-prefix: /tmp/snakemake/local-storage

# SLURM log hygiene
slurm-logdir:                       /scratch/$USER/mosaicatcher_logs/slurm
slurm-keep-successful-logs:         false
slurm-delete-logfiles-older-than:   30

# Efficiency reporting
slurm-efficiency-report:       true
slurm-efficiency-report-path:  /scratch/$USER/mosaicatcher_logs/slurm_efficiency_report.txt
slurm-efficiency-threshold:    0.8
```
:::
:::

## Closing the loop — efficiency report

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
The `slurm-efficiency-report` flag dumps **per-job CPU / memory utilisation** as a text file at the end of each run. Pair it with a notebook → audit which rules are **over-** or **under-requesting** resources.

```{.python style="font-size: 0.78em;"}
# workflow/scripts/toolbox/slurm_efficiency_analysis.ipynb
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv(
    "slurm_efficiency_report.txt", sep=r"\s+", engine="python"
)
under = df.query("cpu_eff < 0.5 or mem_eff < 0.3")
over  = df.query("mem_eff > 0.95")
# → propose new mem_mb / threads per rule
```

```{.python}
rule index_input_bam:
    resources:
        mem_mb = lambda wc, attempt: 500 * attempt,   # auto-scale
        runtime = 30,
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<div style="background: #d1f2eb; border-left: 4px solid #16A085; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.8em 1em; font-size: 0.82em;">
<i class="mdi mdi-notebook-edit" style="color: #16A085; font-size: 1.4em;"></i>

<b>workflow/scripts/toolbox/slurm_efficiency_analysis.ipynb</b>

Reads the efficiency report, groups by rule, plots CPU & RAM efficiency distributions, flags rules below `slurm-efficiency-threshold`, and proposes new `set-resources:` overrides.

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
<i class="mdi mdi-check" style="color: #16A085;"></i>&nbsp; right-size `mem_mb`<br/>
<i class="mdi mdi-check" style="color: #16A085;"></i>&nbsp; right-size `threads`<br/>
<i class="mdi mdi-check" style="color: #16A085;"></i>&nbsp; spot starved I/O rules<br/>
<i class="mdi mdi-check" style="color: #16A085;"></i>&nbsp; feeds back into profile
:::
</div>

::: {style="margin-top: 0.5em; font-size: 0.72em; color: #7f8c8d;"}
Loop: <b>run → report → notebook → updated `set-resources` → run</b>
:::
:::
:::

## What's still on the table {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Could be enabled when ready:**

```{.yaml}
# Cross-workflow caching
# export SNAKEMAKE_OUTPUT_CACHE=...

# Job arrays (v9 plugin)
slurm-array-jobs: all
slurm-array-limit: 1000

# QoS / priority
slurm-qos: normal

# Requeue preempted jobs automatically
slurm-requeue: true
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Useful SLURM plugin knobs not yet used:**

- `slurm-status-command: sacct|squeue`
- `slurm-init-seconds-before-status-checks`
- `slurm-pass-command-as-script`
- `slurm-exclude-failed-nodes`
- `slurm-partition-config` (dynamic partition pick)
- `slurm-jobname-prefix`

## When does each fit? {visibility="uncounted"}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #1F3A5F;"><i class="mdi mdi-snake"></i>&nbsp; Snakemake fits when…</h4>

- Team is <i class="mdi mdi-language-python"></i> Python-native
- Pipeline is **file / target-driven**
- You want the **DAG up-front**
- Debugging needs interactive Python
- One Snakefile, readable end-to-end
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
<h4 style="color: #1F3A5F;"><i class="mdi mdi-source-branch"></i>&nbsp; Nextflow fits when…</h4>

- Team has Groovy / JVM people
- Pipeline is **stream / event-driven**
- **AWS Batch** or **Fusion** matter
- You want **nf-core** off-the-shelf
- You want **Seqera Platform** observability
:::
:::
